learning_outcomes.text: Comprehends the phenomena of electric charge and electrification.
Analyzes the force, electric field, etc., created by charged systems.
Knows the application areas of capacitors in technology and designs capacitor circuits.
Comprehends the formation of magnetic field and magnetic field force.
Applies electromagnetic induction, Faraday's and Lenz's laws in electric circuits.
Analyzes alternating current and direct current circuits.
Learns and applies the rules to be followed in the laboratory and occupational health and safety principles.

syllabus_topics: Rules to be followed in the Laboratory, Occupational Health and Safety Principles, Determination of Laboratory Rules
Electric Field and Gauss's Law, Experiment 1: PARALLEL PLATE CAPACITORS AND DIELECTRIC MATERIALS
Capacitance and Capacitors, Properties of Dielectrics, Experiment 2: KIRCHHOFF'S RULES AND WHEATSTONE BRIDGE
Direct Current Circuits, Experiment 3: DETERMINATION OF RC TIME CONSTANT
Magnetic Field Sources, Experiment 4: MAGNETIC FIELD AT THE CENTER OF A CURRENT-CARRYING WIRE LOOP
Electromagnetic Induction, Self-Inductance, Experiment 5: TRANSFORMERS AND INDUCTION COIL
Alternating Current Circuits (RL and RC Circuits)
assessment_rules: The overall assessment is based on midterm activities (40%) and a final exam (50%). Midterm activities comprise a short quiz (10%) and a performance task for the laboratory (30%). Occupational Health and Safety contributes 0% to the overall grade.
